summary: Backend-only verification of the 37 FOREIGN KEY constraints migration (init_db.py DDL-only change). Ran /app/backend/tests/test_iter104_fk_constraints.py — 38/38 tests PASSED (full-file run 5m11s; also run in 3 prioritised chunks: 11 + 22 + 5, all green). Coverage by requested priority: P1 meeting-delete cascade — created a meeting via POST /api/meetings/ with transcript/analysis/audio_file/meeting_prep/audit_log seeded plus review_edits+reviewer_comments created through the API (PUT /review/{id}/summary, POST /review/{id}/comments), signed it off, then DELETE /api/meetings/{id} → 200 and all 7 child tables at 0 rows, no FK violation, no orphans; a pure raw-SQL `DELETE FROM meetings` (bypassing the app cascade loop) also cascaded all 7 children, proving the constraint itself works; deleting an org_setting holding a team + a meeting did NOT delete the meeting (no over-cascade) and left meetings.team_id/setting_id NULL. P2 SET NULL — created setting(manager_user_id)+team(supervisor_user_id)+staff member, DELETE /api/org/teams/{id} → 200 with staff.team_id and supervisor.team_id NULL; DELETE /api/org/settings/{id} → 200 with all three users' setting_id NULL; DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} for a user simultaneously referenced as team supervisor, setting manager and schedule staff → 200, hard delete, all three FK columns NULL, schedule row survived (no over-cascade); active user still soft-deactivated (is_active=false). P3 role smoke — admin/manager/attendee logins (MFA bypassed per test_credentials.md), 4 common GETs x 3 roles + 9 admin/manager GETs (/dashboard/, /meetings/, /org/structure, /admin/users, /admin/people-stats, /admin/team-insights, /admin/stats, /admin/standards, /admin/standards/documents, /schedules/, /schedules/due, /prep/focus-topics) all 200, zero 500s; meeting detail + /review/{id}; full setting/team CRUD; standards doc upload+delete; focus-topic CRUD. P4 negative — raw SQL INSERTs with bogus org_id / meeting_id / setting_id / staff_user_id all rejected with asyncpg ForeignKeyViolationError and nothing persisted; schema audit confirms exactly 37 public FKs with the exact expected CASCADE/SET NULL action each, and confirms the 7 deliberately-excluded relationships are still unconstrained. P5 — /api/admin/export-evidence and /api/admin/export-transcripts return valid %PDF for a 2-meeting batch, POST /review/{id}/share with 2 users returns 200 with both in shared_with, GET /org/structure count matches DB. Also: super-admin created a throwaway org, seeded one row in all 19 org-scoped tables, DELETE /api/super-admin/orgs/{id} → 200, every row gone, and row counts in the real Test Company org byte-identical before/after (no cross-org blast radius). Post-run: 0 TEST_iter104 residue rows, 0 orphans on any constrained column, login_attempts cleared, and no ERROR/500 in backend logs during the whole test window (the 3 pre-existing 500s in backend.out.log are from the start of the log / older code revision, per iteration_103).

minor.issue: Each DO block only swallows `duplicate_object`. On any environment whose data still has orphans in a newly-constrained column, ADD CONSTRAINT raises foreign_key_violation, which is NOT caught → init_db fails → backend won't boot. Preview is clean (verified 0 orphans), but a fresh/production DB is unverified. Consider ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID (+ later VALIDATE) or pre-cleanup/SET NULL statements per relationship.

Perf-only: several newly-constrained child columns have no supporting index, so each parent DELETE seq-scans the child table: review_edits.org_id (204 rows), standards_entries.org_id (239), audit_logs.org_id (65), meetings.team_id/setting_id/schedule_id (18), teams.supervisor_user_id, org_settings.manager_user_id, schedules.staff_user_id/meeting_type_id, transcripts/analyses/audio_files/meeting_prep/settings/invitations .org_id. Negligible at current volumes; add composite/single-col indexes before tables grow.

The one-time `DELETE FROM audit_logs WHERE ... NOT EXISTS` now runs on every process startup. Harmless and cheap today, but it is a permanent unconditional write on boot — worth gating or moving to a versioned migration.

action_items: Nothing blocking — 38/38 passed, 0 regressions, 0 orphans, no 500s. The FK migration behaves exactly as the app's manual cascade/unassign logic.
Optional hardening: make the FK ADD CONSTRAINT blocks tolerant of pre-existing orphans (NOT VALID, or explicit pre-cleanup) so a dirty non-preview DB cannot brick backend startup.
Optional perf: add indexes on the un-indexed FK child columns listed under minor issues (run `python3 tests/_iter104_fk_index_probe.py` for the live list).
critical_code_review_comments: The 3-row audit_logs DELETE and the 37 ADD CONSTRAINTs live in SCHEMA_SQL, which executes on every boot. That is fine while idempotent, but there is no migration-version table, so any future non-idempotent DDL added here will silently re-run. Recommend introducing a schema_migrations table before the next DDL round.

Exclusions are correct and now regression-locked: jobs.meeting_id, invitations.user_id, meetings.created_by/sign_off_manager_id and the 3 reverse pointers (transcript_id/analysis_id/audio_file_id) are asserted to be UNconstrained by test_deliberately_excluded_relationships_are_not_constrained — the known orphan counts today are jobs.meeting_id=1, invitations.user_id=1, meetings.sign_off_manager_id=4, meetings.created_by=0.

meetings.setting_id/team_id are SET NULL while the app's delete_setting() also nulls them manually — verified consistent (meeting survives, both columns NULL). No double-handling bug, but the app-side loops are now redundant and could be simplified in a future cleanup.
seed_data_creation: All transient and cleaned up: temp meetings (TEST_iter104_lifecycle/raw/setmeet/exp_*), temp org_settings/teams/meeting_types/schedules, 5 temp users (TEST_iter104_*@example.com), 1 throwaway organisation + its user (deleted via super-admin API). Post-run script confirms 0 TEST_iter104 rows across 21 tables, 0 orphans on constrained columns, login_attempts empty.
test_credentials: Used /app/memory/test_credentials.md as-is and all still valid: admin@supervision.com/Admin123!, manager@supervision.com/Manager123! (MFA bypass via DB bcrypt('123456') override), jane@supervision.com/Jane123!, superadmin@1two.one/NewPass123!.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable FK regression gate: `cd /app/backend && python3 -m pytest tests/test_iter104_fk_constraints.py -n 0 -q` (~5m10s, -n 0 mandatory — shared-account MFA override + global login_attempts truncation). It asserts an exact count of 37 public FKs, so ANY future ADD/DROP CONSTRAINT will fail test_all_37_fks_present_with_correct_delete_action until EXPECTED_FKS is updated — that is intentional. Prioritised chunks via -k: 'TestFKSchema or TestNegativeEnforcement or TestMeetingLifecycle' (75s), 'TestOrgStructure or TestUserDeletion or TestScheduleMeetingType or TestSmoke' (180s), 'TestOrgDeletionBlastRadius or TestRegressionEarlierFixes' (76s). Helpers: tests/_iter104_residue.py (residue + global orphan audit), tests/_iter104_fk_index_probe.py (un-indexed FK columns). Note DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} hard-deletes only pending-invite users (must_change_password=TRUE); otherwise it soft-deactivates.
rca_of_the_issue: No issue found. Risk profile of a DDL-only FK addition is (a) a mis-scoped CASCADE deleting more than the app intended, (b) a missing SET NULL turning a previously-200 delete into a 500 FK violation, (c) startup failure from pre-existing orphans. (a) disproved by the over-cascade assertions (schedule survives user delete, meeting survives setting delete, unrelated-org row counts unchanged after a full org delete); (b) disproved by team/setting/user delete flows all returning 200 with the referencing columns NULL; (c) disproved on this DB (0 orphans on all constrained columns, including the 3 audit_logs rows the migration cleans up) but remains a theoretical risk on other environments — flagged as a minor issue.
